integrated_description: Upon receiving a complaint, staff immediately triage for food safety or allergen concerns before any other action; if no safety issue exists, a rapid front-of-house pause is called while a discreet kitchen verification checklist (batch/recipe, holding time/temperature, ticket specs, substitutions, plating) is completed to distinguish execution drift from expectation mismatch. The server, briefed with clear messaging, returns to the guest with an experience-focused apology that does not concede fault, and any remake or comp is framed explicitly as 'restored to our stated standard' rather than an admission of error or an accommodation of personal preference. A documented post-incident review follows: SOPs are adjusted only if execution drift is confirmed, culinary authenticity is never treated as negotiable, and a formal close-the-loop communication is delivered to the guest summarizing the outcome.
integration_rationale: All three modifications converged on the same core constraints — protecting authenticity, avoiding unwarranted fault admission, and separating execution errors from expectation mismatches — making full integration achievable by sequencing the safety triage (stakeholder_b) ahead of the verification checklist (stakeholder_a, stakeholder_c) and binding every remedy and review step to the 'restore to standard' framing shared by all three parties.
